title: Are These the Best 5 Growth Stocks to Buy?
creator: Asymmetric Investing
summary: Asymmetric Investing walks through five growth stocks that are all current holdings in his asymmetric portfolio, arguing they remain long-term compounders after a rough 2026 marked by multiple compression. 1) SoFi (SOFI): shares down 44% but revenue up 41% YoY; lending and financial-services revenue strong, though the technology-platform business weakened after losing Chime as a customer in late 2025. Price-to-book collapsed from ~5 (Sep 2025) to ~1.8, vs big banks at ~2x — the core of the thesis, alongside digital-first scalability and a 35% member CAGR since 2023 (15.8M members, most holding one product, with cross-sell runway). 2) Robinhood (HOOD): down ~29%; maturing from options/crypto 'YOLO' revenue toward net interest and margin revenue, with retirement accounts growing fast and international expansion ahead. Still ~50x earnings and 35x price-to-free-cash-flow; he trimmed a little late last year on stretched valuation but expects 30%+ revenue compounding over a decade. 3) Zeta Global (ZETA): his best 2026 performer (+67%), 34% 3-year revenue CAGR accelerating after the Athena platform launch, operating margin just turning positive; EV/sales ~5, forward P/E ~30. 4) Duolingo (DUOL): contrarian turnaround play, down 56% over the year but up 66% in six months; he dollar-cost-averaged into the position in late 2025 and early 2026. ~18x P/E and 17x P/FCF on 29% revenue growth; engagement (daily active users) is inflecting after 2025 over-monetization hurt growth, and AI tools are expanding product (math, chess) and interactivity. 5) Hims & Hers (HIMS): rough start to 2026 when GLP-1 compounding hit regulatory walls and Novo Nordisk sued, but settled — Novo and Eli Lilly products are now on the platform; management guides 50% revenue growth in H2 2026 after the Eucalyptus/Zava European acquisitions, with EV/sales ~2.8. He frames all five as asymmetric: limited downside, near-unlimited upside. Caption note: auto-generated; 'Dualingo' and 'Himson and Hers' are Duolingo and Hims & Hers; some figures are garbled in places but the five theses are clear.
